business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fitness Biometric Tracking and Wellness Telemetry Apps

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations and Federal statutes; Roman-Germanic legal tradition with cantonal administrative competences)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–United States Treaty concerning the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force 8 May 1991)
Switzerland–People's Republic of China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force 1 March 1986, as amended)
EFTA–China Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland–United Kingdom Trade Agreement (in force 1 January 2021)
Protocol amending the Double Taxation Agreement between Switzerland and Germany (in force 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (SR 955.0), Federal Council Ordinance on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (SR 955.01), FINMA AML Circular and due diligence rules, Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) arts. 620–697 as revised by the company law reform in force as of 1 January 2023, Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411), Criminal Code arts. 305bis and 305ter, and the Federal Act on the International Transfer of Assets (SR 955.0, lex specialis). UBO piercing documentation is compiled in the statutory internal UBO/share register and must be available to the Swiss Federal Audit / FINMA and competent supervisory authorities on request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each shareholder holding more than 25% of the share capital and of each proposed director/authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/identity issuing authority of the individual's country of nationality or residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of no pending criminal record for each director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national or cantonal criminal records authority (e.g., Swiss Federal Criminal Records Office for Swiss residents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official certificate of residence / certified proof of physical address for each authorised signatory and for the administrative office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal population register or national/regional residence registry of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official corporate registry excerpt for any corporate shareholder in the UBO chain
Debt enforcement register excerpt (Betreibungsregisterauszug) for Swiss-resident directors and managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal debt enforcement office (Betreibungsamt) of the director's place of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory AML/CFT screening under AMLA SR 955.0 requires identification of all beneficial owners, verification of identity against an independent authoritative source, and enhanced due diligence for PEPs, including PEP status screening at 25% ownership threshold. Screening must cover the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and the Swiss SECO / State Secretariat for Economic Affairs and National Bank embargo and sanctions lists. Continuous monitoring is required after incorporation; any negative hit requires immediate escalation to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) and a ban on onboarding until cleared by counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) operated by the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and the cantonal commercial register offices; official portal www.zefix.ch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in one of Switzerland's official languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh) or any other language using the Latin alphabet. A name in a non-official language must be accompanied by a precise Swiss-official translation/transliteration and must not be misleading. The legal-form suffix must be in accordance with the chosen corporate form: 'Aktiengesellschaft', 'Société Anonyme', or 'Società Anonima', or the recognised abbreviations 'AG' / 'SA'. The suffix must not be placed at the beginning of the name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Finance / Financial Services / Investment Fund / Fonds
Securities Dealer / Wertpapierhaus / Courtier en valeurs
National Bank / Nationalbank / Swiss National Bank
Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera in combination with federal or state-entity implication
United Nations / UN / World Health Organization / WHO
Cantonal and municipal geographic names (e.g., Zurich, Geneva, Basel, Vaud) when used without express authorisation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name reservation is filed with the relevant cantonal commercial register office after search clearance in Zefix and SHAB. If rejected, the registry issues written reasons. The applicant may within 10 days request reconsideration by the same office with corrected documentation. A formal administrative appeal must be lodged with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 days of service of the rejection notice; thereafter, final judicial review is available through the Federal Administrative Court and the Federal Supreme Court. The reservation may be extended or renewed prior to expiry for up to an additional six months upon proof that incorporation steps are actively ongoing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual-mailbox office is not acceptable as the registered office of a Swiss stock corporation. A professional domiciliation arrangement with a licensed Swiss fiduciary/domiciliation provider is customary and may be acceptable for the low-risk digital health app business, provided the company has a genuine administrative anchor in the domiciliation premises, a locally appointed authorised signatory, and books/records accessible from that Swiss address. The commercial register requires the registered office to be situated in the municipality stated in the articles and must reflect an effective administrative seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but possible: approximately 5%–10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 24 months for a standard, low-risk non-financial software company using an established domiciliation provider. Cantonal commercial register authorities and AML/CFT supervisors retain statutory inspection powers and may visit the registered office without prior warning if the UBO record, books, signatory list, or business activity indicators trigger review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); arts. 629-633 (incorporation procedure); art. 640(2) (minimum capital and paid-up requirement); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV), arts. 14-20; Federal Act on the Commercial Register (Schlussbestimmungen zur OR-Revision).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug), Zuger Kantonsverwaltung, Switzerland.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Gründungsurkunde/Acte constitutif) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts), submitted by a Swiss notary public to the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Aktiengesellschaft requires minimum issued share capital of CHF 100,000. At least CHF 50,000 of the nominal capital must be fully paid up in cash and deposited in a blocked capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a FINMA-supervised bank in Switzerland. A bank certificate confirming the blocked deposit must accompany the registration filing; the funds are released only upon completion of the Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a convened meeting in Zug, the Board of Directors of [Company] AG unanimously resolves: 1. Share Subscription: subscription of 100,000 registered shares of CHF 1.00 nominal is confirmed; aggregate share capital of CHF 100,000 is accepted, and bank certificate evidencing CHF 50,000 liberated capital in escrow is acknowledged. 2. Registered Office: the registered office is fixed at [street address], Zug, Canton of Zug; company purpose per the Articles of Association is adopted. 3. Appointments: [Name] is elected Chairperson with individual signature authority; [Name] is appointed Secretary; [Name] is appointed Financial Officer. 4. Filing: the Board mandates the notary to file registration application with the Commercial Register of Zug and to arrange publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Adoption of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary public licensed in the Canton of Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Articles of Association with corporate purpose restricted to software development and digital health telemetry services. The notary verifies the founders' identities and legal capacity, reads the mandatory provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations, authenticates the deed of incorporation, and issues the notarized instrument. The first board members also sign their acceptance statements at this stage.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of all founders and board members
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts)
Capital subscription declaration signed by each founder
Swiss address/proof of residence of directors
Written consent of the appointed auditor (if required by size)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Formal defects in the deed are cured by a supplementary notarial instrument; missing founder consent is remedied by a notarized power of attorney with legalization/apostille.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-supervised Swiss bank in the Canton of Zug or Zurich.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital deposit account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company-in-formation. Deposit at least CHF 50,000 by wire transfer from a verifiable source of funds. The bank issues a capital confirmation certificate (Freigabebestätigung), which remains blocked until the Commercial Register entry is completed.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application forms
Company name reservation confirmation (via ZEFIX/central name index)
Draft Articles of Association and notarized deed
Source-of-funds declaration to support AML/CDB verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or declines the account, transfer the funds into the notary's client trust account and obtain the notary's capital confirmation instead; re-submit the bank certificate upon account activation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Entry in the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the authenticated deed of incorporation, the Articles of Association, the bank capital confirmation, and the first board resolution to the Register via the electronic e-government filing portal. The Registrar examines statutory legality, capital compliance, and the German/Swiss corporate denomination (AG/SA). Upon approval, the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Bank capital confirmation certificate
First board resolution on appointments and registered office
Signed copy of the Articles of Association
Specimen signatures of authorized board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registrar may issue a query (Rechtspflegeverfahren); respond within 30 days with corrected documents through the notary. If the firm name is refused, file an amended name reservation and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Federal UID, VAT, and Employer Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office via ZEFIX; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); Zug Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV/AVS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Commercial Register entry, the company automatically receives a Federal Business Identification Number (UID/IDE). Separately, apply for voluntary or mandatory VAT registration with the ESTV if the turnover threshold of CHF 100,000 is met. Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office for AHV/IV/EO and supplementary occupational pension (BVG) schemes assuming hiring of personnel.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (dated within 3 months)
UID assignment confirmation
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1)
Shareholder and director identification documents
Employer registration form for AHV/IV/EO and BVG
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID is not automatically issued, request it manually via the ZEFIX portal; for late VAT registration, submit a belated declaration with explanatory note to the ESTV to avoid administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB Publication, Operating Account Activation, and Municipal Office Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC); Municipal Business Licensing Office of the City of Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register automatically publishes the incorporation notice in the SHAB. After publication, the blocked capital deposit is released, the escrow account is converted into an ordinary corporate current account, and the company may begin operations. Submit the municipal business establishment notification to the locality and obtain conformity confirmation of the office premises for the authorized purpose.
required_dossiers: SHAB publication notice
Updated Commercial Register excerpt
Copies of the Articles of Association
Office lease or premises use agreement
Fire safety occupancy approval from the municipal building department
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in the SHAB entry are rectified by an amendment filing; missing municipal clearance is cured by an expedited on-site inspection and administrative fee payment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canton of Zug Department of Economic Affairs (Volkswirtschaftsdirektion) and the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate (kantonale Arbeitsinspektorat); State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for federal labor standards.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required: pure software development and health-fitness telemetry are not licensable activities under Swiss federal law. No Swissmedic marketing authorization applies because the application is a wellness tracker, not a medical device under the Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO). Only a municipal business-establishment notification and office occupancy permit are needed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU), in coordination with the Canton of Zug Environment Directorate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - non-industrial software activity operates from an office; under Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIAO), such digital-services projects are below the EIA screening thresholds. No full EIA report or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing discharges or VOC emissions. Office operations must comply with the Federal Water Protection Act (GSchG) for municipal sewage connection, the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA) for separated waste collection, and the Ordinance on the Return of Electrical Equipment (ORDEE) for disposal of obsolete IT hardware.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal fire safety certification (Feuerpolizei Zug) for office premises; municipal structural inspection and occupancy permit; workplace compliance with the Swiss Labor Act (ArG) arts. 6-7 on health protection and ergonomics, including optional preventive occupational health measures for software personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA); VAT registration portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch (e-services for VAT, 'Mehrwertsteuer-Services' online platform); UID number administered by the Central UID Register (Zefix/eService via www.uid.ch).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Liaison: foreign app operator confirms annual worldwide and Switzerland-source turnover. Step 2 – Obtain Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / CHE-x-xxx.xxx) by filing the UID registration (via www.uid.ch or directly with ESTV when applying for VAT). Step 3 – File VAT registration with ESTV Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer (Formular 5 / online 'Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuerpflicht'), submitting constitutive documents (articles of association, proof of incorporation), foreign tax identification, description of app-based B2C/B2B supplies, bank details and German/French/Italian language designation. Step 4 – ESTV issues VAT number 'CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST' within approximately 15-30 working days; liability commences on the date turnover threshold (CHF 100,000 Swiss-source turnover) was exceeded or on voluntary registration date. Step 5 – Register for return filing cycles (quarterly standard; semi-annual/annual permitted for smaller taxpayers) via ESTV e-channel; maintain 10-year records.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A CH_AG is fully subject to direct federal (8.5% flat pre-tax rate), cantonal and communal income tax; no pass-through treatment. Residence: statutory seat or place of effective management in Switzerland (worldwide unlimited tax liability). For VAT, the AG is an independent taxable person with potential group-VAT grouping under Art. 11 MWSTG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. Available elections (indirect tax): (i) VAT group registration election for closely affiliated entities (Art. 11 and Art. 56 MWSTV; irrelevance of invoicing between group members); (ii) voluntary VAT registration below the CHF 100,000 threshold (Art. 11 para. 1 MGWSTG); (iii) option to tax real estate under Art. 22 MWSTG; (iv) simplified/deemed input-tax methods (saldo method / Art. 37 MWSTV). For direct tax (Stage 4 context): STAF measures – patent box, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction (NID), and 'deemed profit' adjustments for principal/agent structures – operate as elective reliefs, not as flow-through classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) on basis of Mehrwertsteuergesetz (MWSTG) / Loi sur la TVA (LTVA); administered by ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover. For foreign suppliers (including digital app publishers) only Switzerland-source turnover counts; mandatory registration of foreign digital services providers for Swiss B2C supplies once CHF 100,000 turnover from Swiss consumers is exceeded (Art. 10/11 MWSGT; Art. 51-53 MWSTV). Small businesses below threshold may opt in; foreign service suppliers providing only B2B supplies to Swiss businesses normally have no registration obligation (reverse charge applies).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping in Switzerland. Invoicing must contain VAT case data (Art. 26 MWSTG; invoice data: supplier's VAT ID, recipient, date, description, rate, amount of VAT). Federal/technical standards: Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) has replaced legacy payment slips since 1 January 2021; voluntary Peppol BIS e-invoicing and EBICS-based transmission are accepted. A federal proposal for mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is under preparation; no entry-into-force date has been fixed. Cloud/API-based 'real-time clearance' mechanisms are not in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and cross-border services qualify for 0% VAT (exemption with credit of input tax) under Art. 23 para. 1 and 2 MWSTG. For the digital fitness-app activity: (i) B2B supplies of software/licensing/subscription services performed for a foreign recipient are zero-rated if the recipient's business seat/establishment is located abroad and the benefit is received abroad; (ii) B2C tele-app services are placed at the consumer's habitual residence; sales to non-Ch consumers are outside Swiss VAT scope; (iii) sales to Swiss consumers are subject to Swiss VAT at 8.1% unless the platform (Apple/Google) is the liable intermediate. Main conditions: written contract or invoice identifying the foreign customer, no Swiss enumeration (UID) of the recipient, complete export proof retained by supplier for 10 years, and – where services are effectively used within Switzerland – no zero-rating even if invoiced abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Ausfuhrzollanmeldung (NCTS e-declaration via Swiss customs 'e-dec e/declaration') – mandatory for physical goods; for pure digital services no customs declaration applies
Commercial invoice stating the zero-rating provision (Art. 23 MWSTG) and supplier/recipient details
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR or equivalent transport document proving physical departure from Switzerland (for goods)
Service agreement / license or order confirmation evidencing foreign recipient and place of benefit (for software subscriptions and in-app platform commissions)
Proof of foreign business status of the B2B recipient (foreign VAT/Tax ID or equivalent, e.g., EU-VAT ID (Art. 27 MWSTV, Art. 96-101 MWSTV)
Bank payment receipts / ledger statements evidencing cross-border cash flow and in-EU/third-country settlement

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalised, freely convertible currency system covering both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no foreign-currency surrender obligations, no cumulative account balance ceilings, and no profit repatriation limits for direct equity investors. Dividend remittances from an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) are generally subject to a 35% Swiss withholding tax, which may be reduced under double-taxation treaties, but this is a tax matter, not an FX control. The CHF is a globally reserve and freely convertible currency; the SNB does not require licences or pre-approvals for ordinary corporate treasury transactions. Capital movements are broadly unrestricted under the Swiss Foreign Trade and Payments Act (FTPA) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, with very limited emergency power vesting in the Federal Council.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline, mandatory conversion threshold, or surrender requirement applies to export proceeds from the digital fitness-tracker application. The Swiss legal framework does not impose any obligation to convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. The Swiss AG may retain export revenue in the original currency (USD, EUR, GBP, etc.) in multi-currency bank accounts, use it directly for settlement, or convert to CHF through the free interbank market without central-bank notification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) for share capital injection + Operational multi-currency Account (CHF, USD, EUR, GBP)
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account (CHF and major foreign currencies)
Operational Current Account (CHF/UCITS) - capital escrow may be unavailable; separate escrow provider needed for the 50,000 CHF minimum paid-up capital
Operational Account (CHF or multi-currency) and capital escrow capacity through local Raiffeisen member bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury and clearing rails. Switzerland does not belong to the EEA, so a UK, Lithuanian or Irish electronic-money institution (EMI) cannot passport payment services into Switzerland. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise) may offer foreign-currency collection accounts as secondary disbursement channels but are not accepted by the Swiss Commercial Registry as proof of paid-up share capital, and they cannot provide a law-governed Swiss IBAN for payroll, VAT/Federal Tax, or social security (AHV) settlement. For a health-fitness app sold through Apple/Google Billing, using an EMI as an upfront corporate treasury account is functionally viable at a transactional level, but fails the substance test required by Tier-1 Swiss banks; therefore, an EMI should only be used as a pre-funded sub-account for app-store merchant proceeds, with regular sweep settling to the Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding via FINMA-recognised video identification (VideoID) is generally available for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners who hold FATF-compliant residence status and can produce an official passport or national identity card. In practice, Swiss Tier-1 banks require an enhanced due-diligence interview if the parent shareholder is a non-resident company, if a trust is involved, or if controlling directors have no physical work permit in Switzerland. For a company holding health-data rights, banks may require a physical signatory appointment at the bank's head office in Zurich or Geneva, or a sworn mandate authenticated at a Swiss consulate abroad. No absolute statutory mandate exists for face-to-face identity verification under the Swiss AML Ordinance; however, a conservative interpretation for a foreign-managed AG without local economic substance is that physical presence in Switzerland is effective in avoiding onboarding rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The CH_AG shareholder is a non-Swiss corporate entity domiciled in a low-tax or opaque jurisdiction; the ultimate beneficiary is not named in the proposed director mandate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a certified extract from the Swiss Commercial Registry showing the AG's registered address and purpose; (2) a shareholder structure-to-UBO diagram covering all intermediary layers to a natural person; (3) audited financial statements or bank reference of the parent entity for the past three years; (4) legal opinion from a Swiss notary confirming the validity of the share capital transfer; (5) signed capacity certificates for each director and the beneficial owner; and (6) the articles of association clearly defining the health-fitness application activities and the board decision for establishing the Swiss treasury account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital app revenue that cannot be streamed onto bank statements; app-store receivables arrive as pooled Apple/Google payouts, creating commingling/aggregation AML concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ship the bank with the Apple Developer Program merchant agreement and Google Play Console payout profile, alongside a monthly app telemetry summary from the fitness tracker platform. Deflate mixing risk by adding an independent audit trail: generate MT940 balance records from the EMI settlement account, attach copies of Apple and Google remittance advice (including deducted VAT and store commission), and submit a transaction monitoring policy describing the low-risk, consumer-origin payment channel. Include a compliance letter explaining that no peer-to-peer or third-party crypto transfers ever reach the Swiss account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The CEO and product team reside in India/EU/UK while the Swiss AG has no employee contract, pension (AHV) proof, or office lease, triggering 'substance fiction' and criminal admissibility risk under the Swiss Criminal Code Article 251 (forged documentation).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Mitigate with a substance detection letter that includes (1) a Swiss payroll register showing the managing director as an employee with a valid B/L/PE permit; (2) AHV fund certificate and accident insurance (UVG) confirming social security establishment; (3) lease agreement for a physical office in Zug or Geneva with proof of telematic equipment accessible to the controller; (4) board minutes appointing a local authorised signatory who is empowered to execute banking-specific orders; and (5) a transfer-pricing documentation file proving that app development, marketing, and health-data processing functions are charged at arm's length and are not handled by the Swiss board.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Swiss AG's minimum share capital of CHF 100,000 (with at least CHF 50,000 paid up before registration) must be remitted via a compliant SWIFT MT103 from the parent company or ultimate shareholder. The payment instruction must contain Field 70 (Remittance Information) with the following domestic commerce marker: 'Cash capital contribution in accordance with articles of association [Article X] for the purpose of CH_AG registered undertaking.' The Swiss beneficiary bank will require the account to be flagged as an escrow account (Sperrkonto) so that fund release is blocked until the Commercial Registry (Handelsregisteramt) issues the certificate of incorporation. If the shareholder is located in the EU/EEA, a SEPA direct credit (Sepa-Institutszahlung) may be used in EUR, and the SNB reference exchange rate will convert to CHF on value date; however, Tier-1 banks often mandate MT103 for audit, because the SEPA format does not unequivocally identify the originator residual. In strict compliance, the bank will screen the originator against OFAC, EU Consolidated Restrictions, and the Swiss SECO blocker list before clearing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for settlement of operating trade disbursements include the following: (1) SWIFT MT103 (standard credit transfer, single payment) for invoices to suppliers, tax authorities, and individual contractors; (2) SWIFT MT700/MT707 to issue an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP 600) for significant hardware/procurement or clinical trial contracts requiring title documents; (3) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for CHF-denominated disbursements to domestic beneficiaries with same-day laminal value; (4) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR payables to bank accounts in the SEPA region, processed through the Swiss SIC gateway but without charge; (5) Apple iOS App Store and Google Play Billing are not clearing rails themselves; merchant activity is remitted via J.P. Morgan or Bank of America money movement networks, settling in EMEA through SEPA/A Wire and then automatically swept to the Swiss bank via SWIFT MT101 multi-cash. For live transaction processing, the treasury team should set up a multi-currency current account with a concentration account in CHF, using a zero-balance sweeping structure to minimise FX exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (physical delivery) - the primary instrument for hedging CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, and CHF/GBP cash-flow mismatches, subject to standard ISDA 2002 Swiss law documentation with a bilateral credit support annex.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCCY) - allowed for long-term exchange of fixed/floating payment obligations, commonly used when the digital health-app company raises capital in USD and lends to the Swiss operating subsidiary in CHF.

OTC FX options (European exercise) - permitted within the Swiss Banking Act and FINMA circular 2013/7 rules, but require a clean ISDA Score and CSA credit enhancement if used by a company without a financial-market dealer licence.

FX swaps (or forex roll-overs) - used for simultaneous spot and forward legs to manage short-term liquidity between collection currencies (USD from App Store) and disbursement currencies (CHF for Swiss payroll).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - not permissible/not practically available for CHF in onshore Switzerland because the CHF is fully convertible and is not treated as an inconvertible or emerging-market currency; an NDF involving CHF would be considered an artificial restriction and may raise FINMA AML concern over speculative position-taking.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual General Meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulatory filing; approved accounts, voting results and resolutions minuted and retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (Code of Obligations Art. 699); for a 31 December fiscal year-end, on or before 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors risk civil liability for mismanagement; failure to convene the AGM permits shareholders or creditors to petition the competent court for a judicial deadline or dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss federal and cantonal corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration of the registered-office canton, acting for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and the canton
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within the time limit set by the cantonal tax authority, generally six months after the balance-sheet date (usual practice: 30 June of the following year for calendar-year accounts); extension granted on written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000 (approximately USD 11,300), default assessment where no return is filed, late-payment interest, and administrative collection measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value added tax return where annual remittance is authorized by the Federal Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the VAT period; for calendar-year annual filers, due by 1 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest and reminder charges; intentional VAT evasion penalties of up to three times the tax evaded; forfeiture of input VAT deduction for the overdue period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register notification of annual corporate changes arising from the AGM (director and auditor appointments, share capital events)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the relevant shareholder resolution or triggering event; not an unconditional annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration penalties up to CHF 5,000 (approximately USD 5,650); unregistered changes are ineffective against third parties and expose the board to liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit mandatory if the company exceeds two of three thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: CHF 20 million balance-sheet total, CHF 40 million annual turnover, 250 average full-time employees (Art. 727 OR); limited audit mandatory above CHF 500,000 assets, CHF 2 million turnover or 10 employees unless shareholders unanimously waive; companies below all small-company thresholds may fully opt out annually
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Swiss GAAP); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS accepted for consolidated accounts and as a recognized supplementary framework for statutory annual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Since 1 July 2023, Art. 697j OR requires the AG to maintain a confidential beneficial-owner register at the registered office; each shareholder holding at least 25% of shares or votes must declare the beneficial owner, the board must update entries on every share transfer, and the register accuracy must be confirmed at the annual general meeting; no annual UBO filing to a public Swiss authority exists, but the register must be made available to competent tax, AML and law-enforcement authorities upon request
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200 to 8,500 per annum for registered office, commercial address, and corporate administration services in a major Swiss business canton
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800 to 11,000 for a mandated limited audit of a small AG; USD 25,000 to 70,000 for an ordinary audit of a mid-cap AG

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (Swiss federal direct corporate income tax; combined federal/cantonal/communal effective statutory rate varies by canton between approximately 11.9% and 21.1%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland does not grant discretionary tax holidays. Statutory preferential deductions applicable to a digital health/fitness app company include: (i) patent box regime for qualifying IP-derived net income, with up to 90% exemption; (ii) R&D super deduction allowing an additional 50% of eligible Swiss-related R&D expenditure to be deducted; (iii) confirmed capital tax deduction for cantonal/communal capital tax; and (iv) participation exemption for substantial dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen), combining federal and cantonal/communal taxation; filed electronically via the cantonal online tax portal or approved e-filing software (e.g., SwissTax software, E-Zug, eFinance ZH), or in paper form where required by the canton of domicile.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Federal and cantonal corporate income tax returns are filed in one combined return. No separate quarterly corporate income tax return is required; taxpayers remit provisional quarterly installments based on the previous year’s assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate tax return is generally due within six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 30 June for calendar-year companies). Cantonal procedural laws may specify an earlier deadline (e.g., 15 April or 31 July), and extensions are available on written request before the applicable due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, registered office, Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), VAT number, tax subject number, board members, and authorized signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Swiss AG’s details only. The non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner is identified through beneficial ownership schedules, not in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter annual commercial net profit before tax from the statutory financial statements prepared under Swiss GAAP or IFRS, including all income from the fitness app subscription model, in-app purchases, and telemetry data sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Swiss entity’s entire net profit. No apportionment is made for foreign shareholders; the Swiss AG is taxed on its worldwide profit subject to treaty source limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back expenses not tax-deductible under Swiss law, e.g., excessive management fees, related-party royalties lacking arm’s length substance, hidden dividend components, and other non-business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident controlled entities, ensure intra-group management and IT royalty payments are supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing analysis; otherwise the tax authority will add them back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim available deductions: patent box deduction, R&D super deduction, participation exemption, loss carry-forwards, and any treaty-based permanent establishment relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners cannot directly claim Swiss patent box incentives through the AG; the AG must maintain the qualifying IP and substantive activity in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Taxable Profit and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the taxable profit after adjustments, compute federal and cantonal tax due, and enter creditable prepayments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply withholding tax credits and Swiss treaty credits solely against Swiss-source taxable profit; refundable excess credits are not available to non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing triggers reminder fees, then administrative fines (Ordnungsbusse) up to CHF 5,000 at cantonal level and up to CHF 10,000 at federal level. If no return is filed, the tax authority issues a discretionary assessment and may add a surcharge of up to one-third of the assessed tax. Statutory interest accrues on overdue balances at the applicable annual rate (currently approximately 3.5%). There is no prescribed daily surcharge under Swiss federal law.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, withheld from gross distributions to shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss-paying company withholds 35% at source. A non-resident shareholder entitled to treaty relief may apply for a reduced withholding or refund of the excess withholding tax. The beneficial owner must submit a written refund application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) using the relevant treaty refund form (typically Form 82 or 83), accompanied by a current tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority and confirmation of beneficial ownership. The application must be filed within three years of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. Alternatively, the payer may apply to the cantonal tax authority for an advance reduction at source when a prior approval or an attestation from the FTA exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Switzerland imposes no general withholding tax on cross-border royalties under domestic law; many Swiss DTAs provide for a 0% royalty rate, though some treaties cap the rate at 5% or 10%. Interest: Swiss withholding tax of 35% applies only to interest on bonds and money-market instruments issued by Swiss residents. Ordinary bank loans, intercompany loans, and commercial trade debt are not subject to Swiss withholding tax. Under most Swiss DTAs, such interest is exempt from source taxation or is limited to a reduced rate of 0–10% when the beneficial owner is a treaty-resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Switzerland has no explicit statutory threshold for mandatory Local File/Master File documentation. The Swiss Federal Tax Administration’s administrative guidance requires contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where a Swiss taxpayer engages in material cross-border related-party transactions. In practice, formal Local File documentation is expected when controlled transactions exceed CHF 1,000,000 per category on an annual basis; Master File documentation is expected for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above CHF 50,000,000. Below these thresholds, the taxpayer must still maintain sufficient evidence of arm’s length pricing in its audit file.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland is not a jurisdiction subject to the Gulf Cooperation Council Economic Substance Regulations. However, Swiss tax law contains a substantive general anti-abuse rule and substance requirements for treaty entitlement and preferential tax treatment. A Swiss AG must maintain genuine economic activity in Switzerland: real office premises, independent board functions, employees, assets, and actual decision-making support for the digital health and fitness app business. A letterbox or shell company may be denied treaty benefits under the OECD Principal Purpose Test and may lose Swiss participation exemption or patent box relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully submitting an incomplete or inaccurate Swiss corporate income tax return, concealing Apple App Store or Google Play revenues, overstating deductions, or shifting profit through fictitious related-party contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 175 of the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Taxes, a fine of up to 2.5 times the tax evaded is imposed, plus arrears interest and the reassessment of tax. In aggravated cases, the same fine applies for cantonal taxes, and the criminal record reflects a wilful tax offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the false return are subject to individual criminal liability, personal fines, and civil restitution claims. Where the corporate form is used as a sham, piercing the corporate veil permits seizure of personal assets. Travel bans may be requested by investigating authorities in cross-border cases, and serious tax fraud can lead to imprisonment under Swiss criminal procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Swiss AG as a pure letterbox vehicle with no physical office, no employees, no board activity, and no real business substance while claiming treaty benefits or preferential Swiss tax treatment for digital app IP held at the Swiss entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty withholding rate relief, loss of Swiss participation exemption and patent box benefits, cancellation of favourable tax rulings, reclassification of transactions, and imposition of ordinary tax with interest penalties. The FTA may also levy fines for providing false information in tax filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors operate the entity purely as a facade, the corporate veil is pierced for unpaid corporate taxes and fraud claims. Directors face civil restitution to the tax authority, personal liability for unremitted withholding taxes, travel bans pending criminal investigation, and imprisonment where intentional documentary fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG’s payment rails to accept funds derived from criminal conduct, facilitating illegal telemedicine or prescription sales, or processing fraudulent in-app subscriptions that launder crime proceeds through Swiss bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis of the Swiss Penal Code provides imprisonment of up to three years and a fine of up to CHF 500,000 for money laundering. In aggravated cases involving criminal groups, a prison term of up to five years applies. Derivative confiscation of laundered assets is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or negligently fail to prevent the use of corporate bank accounts for money laundering are personally exposed to criminal prosecution. They may also face civil liability for damage caused to investors, asset freezes, travel bans, and disqualification from serving as directors of Swiss companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or constructive dividends to non-resident shareholders without withholding and remitting the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax, or disguising profit distributions as management fees, royalties, or service charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 40 of the Swiss Federal Withholding Tax Act, the taxpayer is liable for a fine of up to 2.5 times the withheld amount evaded, in addition to the payment of the unpaid withholding tax and default interest. Administrative procedures permit seizure of corporate assets for the overdue withholding tax debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid withholding tax if they intentionally or negligently fail to comply with the tax deduction and remittance obligations. This statutory in personam liability pierces the corporate veil, allowing tax authorities to collect directly from directors’ personal assets; travel bans and personal criminal prosecution follow in serious cases.
